author: By Enjoyiana Nururdin
title: Madison spring election: Q&A with District 15 City Council candidate
text: All 20 seats on the Madison City Council are up for election this spring. Ryan Koglin said he has been thinking about running for the City Council for at least 10 years. This spring, Ryan Koglin is running unopposed to represent District 15 on Madison’s City Council.  Local Government Reporter Local Government Reporter All 20 seats on the Madison City Council are up for election this spring. This spring, Ryan Koglin is running unopposed to represent District 15 on Madison’s City Council. The district includes neighborhoods north and east of Lake Monona. District 15’s current alder, Dina Nina Martinez-Rutherford, is on voters’ ballots but has dropped out of the race . To learn more about Madison's City Council races this spring, the Cap Times asked all candidates on voters' ballots to complete a brief survey. Candidates were limited to 800 characters, or about 150 words, per question. Some answers have been edited for length and clarity. For more information about the races on your ballot and voting in the April 1 election, including early absentee ballots, visit myvote.wi.gov . I have lived on the near side for 15 years. I have been active in the SASY Neighborhood Association for 10 years. The past four years I have served as board president. Editor's note: Koglin did not respond to this question. Ryan Koglin said he has been thinking about running for the City Council for at least 10 years. I am running for alder to engage and advocate for the community. I want to create policies that make Madison a place that is affordable, sustainable and safe for everyone. I would bring a systemic approach to the issues. Madison needs to look at issues from numerous perspectives. I love the people in District 15. Affordability. I want to use all the tools the city has to increase housing at all levels. We can use zoning and land use to increase density in areas where transit and amenities are located. Madison needs to reduce the barriers for residents to get involved. Meetings and committees can be at times that are difficult for some people to attend. How can we engage in other ways and reach people where they are at instead of always asking people to come to the city to get engaged. I love the district, the people and what Madison can be if we engage residents and bring more voices to the table to come up with creative solutions. Enjoyiana Nururdin is a local government reporter for the Cap Times. Enjoyiana writes about community, politics, transportation, housing and safety in the Madison region. author: mhubbard@wisctv.com (Meryl Hubbard)
title: Raising flags and resolutions: Madison marks Transgender Day of Visibility
text: Madison Live updates all day, breaking news as it happens and weather every 10 minutes Resize:  Reporter Local leaders and community members are coming together to raise flags and legislation in the spirit of Transgender Day of Visibility. MADISON, Wis. -- Local leaders and community members are coming together to raise flags and legislation in the spirit of Transgender Day of Visibility. "We fly the transgender flag because our city respects individual rights and rejects hate," said Madison Mayor Satya Rhodes-Conway. Mayor Rhodes-Conway stood alongside District 15 Alder Dina Nina Martinez-Rutherford to raise the transgender flag in front of the Madison Municipal Building. "We are powerful, and we are worthy of joy, dignity and love," said Alder Martinez-Rutherford. She’s the first openly trans leader on the Madison Common Council and says she wants to instill joy into a community that’s been facing opposition from the federal government. "If we're not pulling each other closely in times that are hardest, then we have nothing,” said Alder Martinez-Rutherford. Later at the Wisconsin State Capitol, Senator Melissa Ratcliff and Senator Mark Spreitzer introduced a package of bills related to trans advocacy. "Due to the shifting legal landscape at the federal and state level, the timing of this bill to explicitly add legal protections is critical to ensure that our transgender and non-binary communities are protected going forward,” said Senator Spreitzer. One of the bills aims to protect the privacy of individuals who are pursuing a name change to match their gender identity. "This bill will add trans and non-binary people to the list of those who can request a confidential name change under state law," said Senator Ratcliff. Under the bill, those who want to change their name to escape situations of domestic violence could still do so and remain confidential. Both senators say they do not anticipate support from Republicans on this legislation, and that the resolution has been put forward in previous sessions.  ​COPYRIGHT 2025 BY CHANNEL 3000.
